content:
The test image shows longitudinal cross-sections of soybean stems. Key observations:
- Upper stem: cream/light colored pith (appears healthy)
- Lower stems: reddish-brown discoloration throughout the pith/inner tissue
- External stem surface appears mostly intact
- Internal browning pattern

This internal pith browning strongly suggests Brown Stem Rot or Sudden Death Syndrome. Let me check reference images.
Good match - Brown Stem Rot shows brown internal pith discoloration. Now checking Sudden Death Syndrome.
SDS reference shows leaf symptoms - not matching the stem cross-section in test. Checking more Brown Stem Rot and Phytophthora.
Strong match - BSR reference 146 shows longitudinal stem cross-sections with identical brown pith discoloration. Now checking Phytophthora and Fusarium for comparison.
Fusarium shows stem curl/wilt, not matching. One more reference needed - checking Charcoal Rot as another stem disease.

Charcoal Rot shows black microsclerotia - clearly different from the test image.

**Analysis summary:**
- Test image: Longitudinal stem cross-sections showing reddish-brown pith discoloration in lower stems vs cream/healthy pith in upper stem
- Brown Stem Rot references (103, 146): Both show identical brown internal pith discoloration in split stems - strong visual match
- SDS references: Leaf symptoms (interveinal chlorosis/necrosis) - no match
- Phytophthora: External stem wilting - no match
- Fusarium: Stem curl - no match
- Charcoal Rot: Black microsclerotia - no match

The classic diagnostic presentation in the test image (internal pith browning visible only on cross-section, with intact exterior) is the hallmark of Brown Stem Rot.
